desc:
The string pattern has exactly two letters. You must insert exactly one lowercase letter of your choice into s, at any position (including the very beginning or the very end).

Count how many times pattern occurs as a subsequence of the new string, where two occurrences are different if they use different sets of positions. Return the largest count you can reach.

For example, s = "abdcdbc", pattern = "ac" gives 4 (insert an a at the front: 2 letters a times 2 letters c). For s = "aabb", pattern = "ab" the answer is 6, and for s = "abaa", pattern = "aa" it is 6.
constraints: s and pattern consist of lowercase English letters
The answer fits in a 32-bit integer for every allowed input
hints: Only the two letters of pattern can ever help. Which of them is worth inserting, and where?
Inserting the first pattern letter is best at the very front (it pairs with every later copy of the second letter); inserting the second letter is best at the very end.

Count the existing occurrences with one pass (keep the number of first letters seen so far). The answer is that count plus the larger of the two letter totals; if both pattern letters are equal and there are c of them, the answer is c(c+1)/2.
editorial: Inserting a letter that is not part of the pattern changes nothing. Suppose the pattern is xy with x ≠ y. An inserted x forms a new occurrence with every y to its right, so it is best placed in front of everything and creates count(y) new occurrences. Symmetrically, an inserted y at the very end creates count(x) new ones. The result is existing + max(count(x), count(y)), where existing is computed in one scan by adding the number of x seen so far at every y.

If the pattern is xx, the number of occurrences is the number of pairs of positions among the c letters x, which is c(c-1)/2; one more x (anywhere) gives (c+1)c/2. The input bound keeps all values in 32 bits. O(n) time, O(1) space.
